name: Shark Bay, Western Australia
blurb: Seagrass meadows, dugongs, tiger sharks and living stromatolites.

tip.title: Remove the tiger sharks
tip.text: Tiger sharks eat dugongs and green turtles, and make them shift their feeding grounds. Set Tiger shark to -100% and watch grazers rise and the seagrass beds come under pressure.

nodes.desc: Shallow, clear water lets light reach the seagrass beds, and the arid land above gets strong sun year round.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead seagrass, stromatolite mats, carcasses and leaf litter, returning nutrients to the sediment and soil.

nodes.name: Stromatolite-building cyanobacteria
nodes.desc: Microbial mats at Hamelin Pool that trap sediment and cement it with calcium carbonate, building living stromatolites, the most diverse and abundant in the world.
Shark Bay holds roughly 10,000 dugongs. They eat mainly seagrass, especially Halophila and Halodule, and their feeding opens space for fast-growing species to recolonise.

nodes.name: Green turtle
nodes.desc: Adults are mostly herbivorous, grazing seagrass and algae in shallow bays. Green turtles nest on sandy beaches in Shark Bay.
Has the widest diet of any shark, including fish, sea turtles, dugongs and dolphins. Dugongs shift feeding areas when sharks are abundant.

nodes.name: Feral cat
nodes.desc: Introduced predator ranked among the biggest threats to Australian mammals. Removed from Dirk Hartog Island so lost mammals could return.
